Singapore Shipping Corp orders two new car carriers for US$210 mil, may add another two
article:
Singapore Shipping Corporation has contracted Guangzhou Shipyard International Company and China Shipbuilding Trading Company to build two vessels for US$210 million as part of its fleet renewal programme.

SSC may spend up to US$400 million to acquire a total of four vessels, and has received a waiver from SGX on very substantial acquisitions.

SSC's market value, based on its last share price of 28 cents on Nov 20, gives it a market value of just below $118 million.

The company had indicated in its most recent annual report ended March 31 that around 80% of its fleet is approaching "the end of their economic useful lives".

According to SSC, the two new vessels to be built are of each 7,000-CEU Pure Car and Truck Carriers and are to be delivered on or around March 31 2031 and June 30 2031 respectively.

The vessels will incorporate dual-fuel liquefied natural gas propulsion technology, providing greater fuel flexibility and improved emissions performance compared with conventional-fuel vessels.

See also: Nordic Group secures approximately $58.3 million worth of new contracts

From left: William Zhou, president of GSI; Ow Chio Kiat, SSC's executive chairman and Lai Lihua, deputy director, specialized tonnage deptartment of CSTC/ Photo: SSC

SSC plans to fund the vessels via a combination of internal cash resources, bank financing, or even capital markets if "conditions are favourable."

See also: Lincotrade secures $81.1 mil in new contracts in 1QFY2027, order book hits $149.5 mil

"Although the car-carrier market has benefited from favourable supply and demand conditions in recent years, our decision to invest in these vessels is not predicated on the continuation of current market conditions," says executive chairman Ow Chio Kiat.

"Rather, it reflects our recognition that fleet renewal is essential to SSC’s long-term future. Ships are long-life assets, and decisions of this magnitude must be guided by a disciplined assessment of the industry’s long-term prospects rather than short-term market cycles," he adds.

title: Australian opposition calls for changes to gas reservation plan
article:
(Nov 22): Australia’s opposition coalition party has raised more concerns about the government’s plan for liquefied natural gas (LNG) exporters to increase supply to the domestic market, ahead of the legislation being voted on this week.

The government wants to force LNG exporters to reserve as much as a 20% of their supply for the local market from 2028, requiring major global producers to ensure more is available for Australian consumers. On Saturday, the government said negotiations were continuing.

Speaking on News 24 on Sunday, Susan McDonald, the shadow minister for resources and northern Australia, said she was concerned about the amount of ministerial intervention allowed under the proposed domestic gas reservation scheme.

“Legislation should not be subjective,” McDonald said. “It should be really clear and transparent, particularly if you try to encourage multibillion dollar investments to extract cash resources from under the ground.”

McDonald also highlighted worries about reciprocal responsibilities, clarity around the carve-out for the state of Western Australia and the issue of oversupply in the market. “The risks of getting this wrong, particularly for the domestic companies in the south of the country is very great,” she said.

The oil and gas sector has strongly opposed key elements of the planned reform including requiring exporters to sell gas below cost, which has been backed by unions and business groups.Despite being one of the world’s biggest LNG exporters, Australia faces a shortfall on its more densely populated eastern coast towards the end of this decade. The government’s legislation is designed to help address the deficit and to shield domestic consumers from high international prices.

See also: South Korea to ground flights, delay trading for college exam

McDonald said she had been working with the government on “a very tight range of issues” and that she was optimistic they could be resolved this week.
